newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Mobutu sets up in north Moroccan hotel.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu sets up in north Moroccan hotel.

text.p: Ousted leader of Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko arrived on Wednesday in a north Morocco sea resort where he is expected to spend up to six weeks.
A hotel worker at Le Mirage Hotel, at Cap Spartel resort north of Tangier, told Reuters: "King Hassan's guest (Mobutu) arrived at the hotel this afternoon with his family."
The source would give no other details.
At Tangier's Boukhalef airport an official said: "A Zairean delegation arrived on a royal flight from Rabat around 1 p.m. (1300 GMT)."
Airport workers and staff were kept away from the plane and not allowed to see who was in the delegation, the official said.
Earlier on Wednesday a manager in Le Mirage hotel said: "Mobutu and his entourage are expected to spend several weeks here...All hotel rooms have been requisitioned until August 20."
Heavy security was seen around the hotel, and a police officer said: "One of his majesty's (King Hassan's) highest guests is expected to arrive here on Wednesday."
All access to the hotel was barred.
Eyewitnesses said police had been deployed between Tangier airport and the hotel.

Mobutu, who arrived in Morocco on May 23 after being ousted in a rebellion, had been staying at the 30-room Amphitrite hotel, next door to King Hassan's royal palace of Skhirat, 20 km (12 miles) south of Rabat.
Eyewitnesses said later on Wednesday that the heavy security around this hotel had been lifted. The hotel would be open again to the public on Thursday.
When Mobutu arrived in Morocco on May 23, he was accompanied by a group of more than 30 people including his family, an official source said at the time.
Located on a cliff overlooking the Mediterranean Cap Spartel beach, Le Mirage has about 20 rooms and steps giving direct access to the sea.
Asked by Reuters about Mobutu's final destination such as Portugal, a Zairean member of Mobutu's entourage said: "I do not know whether Mobutu will leave for Portugal or elsewhere."
Earlier, diplomats said Mobutu might leave Morocco for Portugal after a short stay in France for medical treatment.
It was not known why Mobutu was moving from near Rabat.
Moroccan officials were not immediately available for comment and there were no reports by the official media.
